description.short_caption: Erythema and swelling of the lower leg, suggestive of cellulitis.
description.detailed_description: This image shows the lower legs of a patient, with the right leg prominently displaying diffuse erythema, swelling, and a shiny appearance. The redness extends from the ankle to the mid-calf region. The left leg appears unaffected in comparison. The findings are consistent with an inflammatory or infectious process, such as cellulitis.
visible_findings: diffuse erythema of the right lower leg
clear demarcation of redness extending to mid-calf

description.short_caption: Erythema and swelling of the lower leg.
description.detailed_description: This image shows the lower leg of a patient with visible erythema and mild swelling. The skin appears shiny, with a reddish discoloration extending along the anterior aspect of the leg. There are no visible breaks in the skin or ulcerations. The findings suggest a possible inflammatory or infectious process, such as cellulitis.
visible_findings: no visible skin breaks or ulcerations

Case_12003/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Growth on a Thayer-Martin subculture plate.

description.short_caption: Bacterial growth on a Thayer-Martin agar plate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Thayer-Martin agar plate with visible bacterial growth. The colonies appear small, round, and translucent to slightly opaque, distributed along the streak lines. The agar has a reddish-brown color, characteristic of the medium, which is selective for Neisseria species. The growth pattern suggests successful isolation of an organism, likely from a clinical specimen.
visible_findings: small, round, translucent to slightly opaque colonies

Case_12003/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Anal culture on JEMBEC agar plate.

description.short_caption: Bacterial colonies on JEMBEC agar plate from an anal culture.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a JEMBEC agar plate with multiple bacterial colonies of varying sizes and morphologies. The colonies are distributed across the plate, with some appearing smooth and others more irregular. The agar is a reddish-brown color, consistent with the medium used for culturing specific organisms. The central well suggests the use of a CO2-generating system, typical for JEMBEC plates.
visible_findings: multiple bacterial colonies of varying sizes

Case_12003/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of organism, under oil at 100x magnification.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci in clusters, under oil immersion at 100x magnification.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain viewed under oil immersion at 100x magnification. The organisms appear as gram-positive cocci, characterized by their purple coloration and arrangement in clusters. The background is clear, with no visible host cells or debris, suggesting a pure bacterial sample.
